babs.3: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe
babs.5: Feeding others is part of Islam
babs.6: It is part of faith to love for one's brother what one loves for oneself
babs.7: Love of the Messenger ﷺ is part of faith
babs.9: A sign of faith is love of the Anṣār
babs.11: Fleeing from trials is part of the religion
babs.12: The Prophet's ﷺ saying: "I know Allah best among you"
babs.13: It is part of faith to hate returning to disbelief as one hates being thrown into the Fire
babs.14: The believers differ in rank according to their deeds
babs.16: "But if they repent, establish the prayer and give the zakāt, then let them go their way"
babs.17: Whoever says that faith is action
babs.18: When Islam is not held in truth
babs.19: Spreading the greeting of peace is part of Islam
babs.20: Sins belong to the ways of the Jāhiliyya, and one who commits them is not declared a disbeliever for it, except through associating partners with Allah
babs.21: "And if two groups of the believers fight, make peace between them"
babs.24: Standing in prayer on the Night of Decree is part of faith
babs.26: Voluntary night prayer in Ramaḍān is part of faith
babs.27: Fasting Ramaḍān seeking reward is part of faith
babs.30: The excellence of a person's Islam
babs.31: The most beloved religious practice to Allah is the most constant
babs.32: The increase and decrease of faith
babs.34: Following funeral processions is part of faith
babs.35: The believer's fear that his deeds may be nullified without his realising it
babs.36: Jibrīl asking the Prophet ﷺ about faith and Islam
babs.38: The virtue of one who safeguards his religion
babs.39: Paying the fifth is part of faith
babs.40: What has come about deeds being by intention
babs.41: The Prophet's ﷺ saying: "The religion is sincere counsel (naṣīḥa)"

8.matn: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Hanzala ibn Abi Sufyan informed us, from ʿIkrima ibn Khalid, from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Islam is built upon five: bearing witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving the zakat, the pilgrimage, and fasting Ramadan.”
8.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Islam is likened to a building resting on five supporting pillars. In Fath al-Bari, Ibn Hajar explains that al-Bukhari opens the Book of Faith with this hadith because it shows that deeds are part of faith.

9.matn: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAmir al-ʿAqadi narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Dinar, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Faith has sixty-some branches, and modesty (haya') is a branch of faith.”
9.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Faith includes many attitudes and deeds, not only an inner conviction. Modesty is mentioned specifically because it holds a person back from what is bad.

10.matn: Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi s-Safar and Ismaʿil, from ash-Shaʿbi, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe, and the emigrant (muhajir) is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden.” Abu ʿAbd Allah (al-Bukhari) said: Abu Muʿawiya said: Dawud narrated to us, from ʿAmir, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. And ʿAbd al-Aʿla said: from Dawud, from ʿAmir, from ʿAbd Allah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
10.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The complete Muslim harms no one by word or deed. Emigration is related to its inner meaning: leaving what Allah has forbidden. The two additional chains at the end show that ash-Shaʿbi (ʿAmir) heard the hadith from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr.

11.matn: Saʿid ibn Yahya ibn Saʿid al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Abu Burda ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Burda narrated to us, from Abu Burda, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: They said: “O Messenger of Allah, which Islam is best?” He said: “The one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.”
11.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The question concerns the best quality of a Muslim. The answer puts not harming others in word and deed first.

12.matn: ʿAmr ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to us, from Yazid, from Abu l-Khayr, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, may Allah be pleased with them both: A man asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Which Islam is best?” He said: “That you feed others and give the greeting of peace to those you know and those you do not know.”
12.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Here kindness towards others is emphasised: feeding people and greeting all Muslims, not only acquaintances. The different answers to similar questions are usually explained in the commentaries by the situation of the questioner or listeners.

13.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Qatada, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. And from Husayn al-Muʿallim, who said: Qatada narrated to us, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “None of you (truly) believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.”
13.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: What is negated here is the completeness of faith, not faith itself. It means wishing for one's brother the good one wishes for oneself.

14.matn: Abu l-Yaman narrated to us, saying: Shuʿayb informed us, saying: Abu z-Zinad narrated to us, from al-Aʿraj, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “By Him in Whose hand my soul is, none of you (truly) believes until I am more beloved to him than his father and his child.”
14.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Love for the Prophet ﷺ is part of faith and should stand above love for one's closest relatives. It shows itself in following his Sunna.

15.matn: Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace (change of chain). And Adam narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Qatada, from Anas, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “None of you (truly) believes until I am more beloved to him than his father, his child and all people.”
15.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: This version adds “all people” to the previous one. The sign (h) marks in the transmission the switch to a second chain leading to the same wording.

16.matn: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab ath-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilaba, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Three (qualities) – whoever has them finds the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are more beloved to him than anything else, that he loves a person only for Allah's sake, and that he hates to return to disbelief as he would hate to be thrown into the Fire.”
16.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The “sweetness of faith” describes inner joy in obedience. The three qualities concern love of Allah and His Messenger, love for Allah's sake, and aversion to disbelief.

17.matn: Abu l-Walid narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Jabr informed me, saying: I heard Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The sign of faith is love of the Ansar, and the sign of hypocrisy is hatred of the Ansar.”
17.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The Ansar received the Prophet ﷺ in Medina and supported him. Whoever loves them for this support thereby shows his faith.

18.matn: Abu l-Yaman narrated to us, saying: Shuʿayb informed us, from az-Zuhri, who said: Abu Idris ʿA'idh Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah informed me that ʿUbada ibn as-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him – who had taken part in Badr and was one of the representatives (nuqaba') on the night of al-ʿAqaba – reported: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, while a group of his companions was around him: “Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, not steal, not commit fornication, not kill your children, not bring forth a slander you invent between your hands and feet, and not disobey in what is right. Whoever of you fulfils (it), his reward is with Allah. Whoever commits any of that and is punished for it in this world, it is an expiation for him. And whoever commits any of that and then Allah conceals it, his matter is with Allah: if He wills He pardons him, and if He wills He punishes him.” So we pledged allegiance to him on that.
18.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The report names contents of the pledge. It shows that the punishment carried out in this world for these offences is an expiation, and that the outcome rests with Allah when the sin remained hidden.

19.matn: ʿAbd Allah ibn Maslama narrated to us, from Malik, from ʿAbd ar-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd ar-Rahman ibn Abi Saʿsaʿa, from his father, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Soon the best wealth of a Muslim will be sheep with which he follows the mountain tops and the places of rainfall, fleeing with his religion from trials.”
19.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The hadith concerns times of trial in which religion is endangered within society. Then withdrawal in order to preserve one's religion may be preferable.

20.matn: Muhammad ibn Salam narrated to us, saying: ʿAbda informed us, from Hisham, from his father, from ʿA'isha, who said: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded them, he commanded them deeds they were able to do. They said: “We are not like you, O Messenger of Allah; Allah has forgiven you your past and future sins.” Then he became angry until the anger could be seen in his face. Then he said: “The most God-fearing of you and the most knowing of Allah is I.”
20.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The Prophet ﷺ taught moderation in worship. His anger was directed at the idea that excess is better than his Sunna; knowledge of Allah shows itself in the heart, not only in the quantity of deeds.

21.matn: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Qatada, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Three (qualities) – whoever has them finds the sweetness of faith: one to whom Allah and His Messenger are more beloved than anything else, one who loves a servant (of Allah) only for Allah's sake, and one who hates to return to disbelief – after Allah has saved him from it – as he would hate to be cast into the Fire.”
21.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: A further chain for hadith no. 16 with the addition “after Allah has saved him from it”. Al-Bukhari places it under a separate chapter on aversion to disbelief.

22.matn: Ismaʿil narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to me, from ʿAmr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, from his father, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The people of Paradise will enter Paradise and the people of the Fire the Fire. Then Allah, the Exalted, will say: ‘Bring out whoever has in his heart faith the weight of a mustard seed.’ So they will be brought out, having already turned black, and cast into the river of al-Haya or al-Hayat – Malik was unsure – and they will sprout as a seed sprouts at the edge of a torrent. Do you not see that it comes out yellow and twisted?” Wuhayb said: ʿAmr narrated to us: “al-Hayat”, and he said: “a mustard seed of good”.
22.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The hadith shows that faith increases and decreases and that even a small amount of it saves in the end. The remark at the end records differences in the wording of the narrators.

23.matn: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Umama ibn Sahl, that he heard Abu Saʿid al-Khudri say: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “While I was asleep, I saw people being presented to me wearing shirts; some reached the chest and some were shorter. And ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab was presented to me wearing a shirt that he was dragging.” They said: “How did you interpret that, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “The religion.”
23.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: In the dream the shirt stands for religion, which covers and protects a person. The different lengths show that believers differ in their religion; the dream also contains a merit of ʿUmar.

24.matn: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Anas informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah, from his father: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by a man of the Ansar who was admonishing his brother about modesty. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Leave him, for modesty is part of faith.”
24.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The man was reproaching his brother because his modesty made him reserved. The Prophet ﷺ made clear that modesty is a quality of faith.

25.matn: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Musnadi narrated to us, saying: Abu Rawh al-Harami ibn ʿUmara narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Waqid ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard my father narrate from Ibn ʿUmar: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish the prayer and give the zakat. If they do that, they have protected their blood and their wealth from me, except by the right of Islam, and their reckoning is with Allah.”
25.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhari places the hadith under the chapter on the verse “But if they repent, establish prayer and give zakat, let them go their way” (9:5). Ibn Hajar explains that “the people” refers to the idolaters and that blood and wealth are protected by Islam; Allah judges what is inward.
